title: Parse CSV text
prompt:
Implement `parseCsv(text, options)` in `src/csv.js` (it is a stub that throws). It returns an array of rows, each row an array of strings. `options.delimiter` is a single character, default `,`; if it is not a string of length one, or is a double quote, ` ` or ` `, throw `RangeError('delimiter must be one character other than a quote or a line break')`. If `text` is not a string throw `TypeError('text must be a string')`. Rules (RFC 4180): fields are separated by the delimiter; a row ends at ` ` or ` `, while a lone ` ` is not a line break and stays in the field; nothing is trimmed. A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it can contain the delimiter, line breaks (kept exactly as written) and `""` for one literal quote, and it ends at the next single `"`. An empty field is the empty string. A leading byte order mark (`﻿`) is removed before parsing. The final line break does not start another row, so `'a,b '` is `[['a','b']]`; empty `text` returns `[]`; a blank line anywhere else is a row with one empty string, `['']`; a trailing delimiter gives a trailing empty field. Errors are `SyntaxError`s: input that ends inside a quoted field gives `unterminated quoted field`; a `"` inside an unquoted field gives `unexpected quote at position

`; and any character other than a delimiter, a line break or the end of the input directly after a closing quote gives `unexpected character at position

`. `

` is the 0-based index of the offending character in the text after the byte order mark has been removed. Run `npm test` to check your work.

origin.note: Spike task. Behaviour follows RFC 4180 with explicit error messages so that failure behaviour is fully specified.
